name: CI

on:
  push:
    # The train tests the merged tree; a lane can opt in early with ci.sh --full.
    branches: [main, 'ci/batch-*', 'ci/full/*']
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

# A newer push to the same branch or pull request cancels the run before it.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  # Per branch, so lanes never cancel each other; a lane's newer candidate
  # (or a pull request's newer push) cancels its older run, main's never.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/ci/') }}

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0

jobs:
  # Decides which jobs this change needs (.github/scripts/ci_gate.py): by
  # the paths that changed, and not at all when the same tree already
  # passed CI, Engine E2E and Windows. Its summary says why each job runs.
  gate:
    name: what to run
    # Same-repo snapshots are tested by the train. Keep fork PR checks.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      portable: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.portable }}
      check: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.check }}
      motion: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.motion }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 0 || 2 }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: python3 .github/scripts/ci_gate.py ci

  # Everything that doesn't need a Mac, on ubuntu (macOS runners are the
  # scarce ones): fmt, the scans, and clippy and tests for the crates with
  # no macOS-specific code.
  portable:
    name: fmt, scans, portable crates (ubuntu)
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.portable != 'skip'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      MODE: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.portable }}
    steps:
      - name: Gate mode
        # Fail closed: a job that runs without a mode from the gate would
        # skip every step and pass without checking anything.
        run: |
          case "$MODE" in
            full|warm) ;;
            *) echo "::error::the gate gave this job no valid mode ('$MODE'); not passing without running"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Rust toolchain
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --component rustfmt,clippy
          rustup default stable
          rustc --version
          cargo --version

      - name: Cargo cache
        id: cache
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2
        with:
          key: ci-portable
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Format
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        run: cargo fmt --all --check

      - name: PR description checks (unit tests)
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        run: python3 .github/scripts/pr_checks_test.py

      - name: Merge train (isolated Git and fake GitHub)
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        run: python3 scripts/tests/train_sim.py

      - name: Third-party notices up to date
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        run: scripts/third-party-notices.sh --check

      - name: Clippy portable crates
        if: env.MODE == 'full' || steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p isocast-ipc -p isocast-mux -p isocast-obsws -p isocast-remote -- -D warnings

      - name: Test portable crates
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        run: cargo test --locked -p isocast-ipc -p isocast-mux -p isocast-obsws -p isocast-remote

  check:
    name: clippy, test (macOS arm64)
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.check != 'skip'
    # GitHub-hosted only: pull requests from forks must never run on our own
    # machines, so no self-hosted runners here.
    runs-on: macos-15
    # A cold cache (a ci/** candidate, or main after a failed run, which
    # saves no cache) needs ~29 min of clippy and ~28 of tests before the
    # contract and docs steps: 60 cut one off at 61 min (2026-10-22).
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      # full; docs (reference docs only); warm (main: build only on a cache miss).
      MODE: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.check }}
    steps:
      - name: Gate mode
        # Fail closed: a job that runs without a mode from the gate would
        # skip every step and pass without checking anything.
        run: |
          case "$MODE" in
            full|docs|warm) ;;
            *) echo "::error::the gate gave this job no valid mode ('$MODE'); not passing without running"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4

      - name: Rust toolchain
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal --component rustfmt,clippy
          rustup default stable
          rustc --version
          cargo --version

      - name: Cargo cache
        id: cache
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2
        with:
          # Only main writes the cache; pull requests read it. Docs mode
          # builds only the CLI: saving that would leave a thin cache.
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && env.MODE != 'docs' }}

      - name: Clippy
        if: env.MODE == 'full' || (env.MODE == 'warm' && steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true')
        # The portable job lints and tests the excluded crates on ubuntu.
        run: cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --exclude isocast-ipc --exclude isocast-mux --exclude isocast-obsws --exclude isocast-remote -- -D warnings

      - name: Test
        if: env.MODE == 'full' || (env.MODE == 'warm' && steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true')
        run: cargo test --locked --workspace --exclude isocast-ipc --exclude isocast-mux --exclude isocast-obsws --exclude isocast-remote ${{ env.MODE == 'warm' && '--no-run' || '' }}

      - name: Platform clock and pool contracts
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        run: |
          cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -p isocast-platform-contracts -- -D warnings
          cargo build --locked -p isocast-platform-contracts
          python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_platform_contracts.py
          python3 scripts/platform-contracts.py --bin target/debug/isocast-platform-contracts --backend native --suite core --work "$RUNNER_TEMP/platform-contracts"

      - name: CLI, setup and MCP references up to date
        if: env.MODE == 'full' || env.MODE == 'docs'
        run: |
          cargo build --locked -p isocast-cli
          python3 scripts/reference-docs.py target/debug/isocast --check

  motion:
    # The motion harness (docs/motion-testing.md): the real interface drawn
    # offscreen, scripted drags replayed on a virtual clock, every frame
    # checked. Lockstep runs draw the same pixels on any machine, so this
    # is a pass/fail gate, not a benchmark: the harness's controls must
    # come out as expected, and the standard suite must match its baseline
    # of known issues exactly (scripts/motion/suite.toml). The gate runs it
    # when the interface, the compositor or render paths, or the harness
    # change.
    name: build motion binaries (macOS arm64)
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.motion != 'skip'
    runs-on: macos-15
    # A cold release build alone exceeded 60 minutes on run 41849337186.
    # Compile once for both suites, with margin independent of test time.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      MODE: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.motion }}
    steps:
      - name: Gate mode
        # Fail closed: a job that runs without a mode from the gate would
        # skip every step and pass without checking anything.
        run: |
          case "$MODE" in
            full|warm) ;;
            *) echo "::error::the gate gave this job no valid mode ('$MODE'); not passing without running"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Rust toolchain
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal
          rustup default stable

      - name: Cargo cache
        id: cache
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Build release binaries
        if: env.MODE == 'full' || steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: cargo build --locked --release -p isocast-ui -p isocast-daemon -p isocast-cli

      - name: Pack motion binaries (preserve executable permissions)
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        run: tar -C target/release -cf "$RUNNER_TEMP/motion-binaries.tar" isocast isocastd isocast-ui

      - name: Share binaries with both suites
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: motion-binaries
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/motion-binaries.tar
          if-no-files-found: error
          overwrite: true
          retention-days: 14

  motion-tests:
    name: motion suite (${{ matrix.suite }}, headless, macOS arm64)
    needs: [gate, motion]
    if: needs.gate.outputs.motion == 'full'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        suite: [controls, standard]
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4
        with:
          name: motion-binaries
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}

      - run: tar -C "$RUNNER_TEMP" -xf "$RUNNER_TEMP/motion-binaries.tar"

      - name: Harness controls
        if: matrix.suite == 'controls'
        run: scripts/motion.sh --bin "$RUNNER_TEMP" --suite scripts/motion/controls.toml --no-timing --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/motion/controls"

      - name: Standard suite (lockstep)
        if: matrix.suite == 'standard'
        run: scripts/motion.sh --bin "$RUNNER_TEMP" --clock lockstep --no-timing --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/motion/suite"

      - name: Upload results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: motion-results-${{ matrix.suite }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/motion
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          overwrite: true
          retention-days: 14

[package]
name = "isocast-browser-protocol"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
description = "The records an isocast-browser helper sends isocastd (pictures, sound, failures), on every OS."
publish = false

[dependencies]
anyhow = "1.0.104"

[package]
name = "isocast-browser"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
description = "Isocast's browser source renderer: a helper process isocastd starts per page (WebKitGTK 6 on Linux, WebView2 on Windows, offscreen)."
publish = false

[[bin]]
name = "isocast-browser"
path = "src/main.rs"

# Linux and Windows only (elsewhere the binary is a stub). The browser
# engine runs in this process (and its children), never in isocastd: a
# missing library or runtime, a crash or a hang costs one browser source,
# not the engine.
#
# Linux: the system's WebKitGTK 6 and GTK 4 (LGPL, linked dynamically).
[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]
webkit6 = "=0.6.1"
# v4_10: webkit6 needs gtk::Accessible (GTK 4.10; Ubuntu 24.04 has 4.14).
gtk4 = { version = "=0.11.5", features = ["v4_10"] }
libc = "0.2"
base64 = "0.22.1"

# Windows: the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime (preinstalled on Windows 10
# and 11), through webview2-com (MIT; its static loader is Microsoft's
# WebView2 SDK, BSD-3-Clause). The windows crate is the one wgpu and the
# platform crate already lock.
[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]
isocast-browser-protocol = { path = "../isocast-browser-protocol" }
base64 = "0.22.1"
webview2-com = "=0.39.1"
windows-numerics = "0.3.1"
windows = { version = "0.62.2", features = [
    "Foundation",
    "Foundation_Numerics",
    "Graphics",
    "Graphics_Capture",
    "Graphics_DirectX",
    "Graphics_DirectX_Direct3D11",
    "System",
    "UI_Composition",
    "UI_Composition_Desktop",
    "Win32_Foundation",
    "Win32_Graphics_Direct3D",
    "Win32_Graphics_Direct3D11",
    "Win32_Graphics_Dwm",
    "Win32_Graphics_Dxgi",
    "Win32_Graphics_Dxgi_Common",
    "Win32_Graphics_Gdi",
    "Win32_Security",
    "Win32_System_Com",
    "Win32_System_LibraryLoader",
    "Win32_System_Threading",
    "Win32_System_WinRT",
    "Win32_System_WinRT_Composition",
    "Win32_System_WinRT_Direct3D11",
    "Win32_UI_HiDpi",
    "Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging",
] }

version.workspace = true

#!/bin/sh
# Prepare a Mac to be an Isocast test Mac (run there, from the synced
# checkout, by `scripts/testmac.sh setup` and `scripts/testmac.sh desktop`).
#
#   testmac-setup.sh tools     Rust, ffmpeg, a numpy venv, the signing
#                              keychain and the desktop-session bridge.
#                              Safe to run again.
#   testmac-setup.sh desktop   EC2 Macs only (needs passwordless sudo): grow
#                              the disk to the EBS volume, give the user the
#                              password read from stdin, turn on screen
#                              sharing and automatic login, never sleep or
#                              lock, then reboot into the desktop session
#                              (the bridge loads at login).
#
# Privacy grants (screen recording, camera, microphone, cua-driver's
# Accessibility) still need a person at the desktop once, over Screen
# Sharing; see "Test Mac" in docs/archive/2026-10-22/notes.md.
set -eu

keys="$HOME/.config/isocast-testmac"
keychain="$keys/signing.keychain-db"
scratch="$HOME/isocast-scratch"

tools() {
    export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
    if ! command -v rustup >/dev/null; then
        curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal -c clippy,rustfmt
    fi
    rustup update stable >/dev/null
    rustup component add clippy rustfmt >/dev/null
    command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null || HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew install ffmpeg >/dev/null
    mkdir -p "$scratch/main"
    [ -x "$scratch/main/venv/bin/python" ] || {
        python3 -m venv "$scratch/main/venv"
        "$scratch/main/venv/bin/pip" -q install numpy
    }

    # Over SSH the login keychain stays locked, so dev apps are signed from
    # a keychain of our own with a self-signed identity; privacy grants are
    # tied to that certificate and survive rebuilds.
    mkdir -p "$keys"
    chmod 700 "$keys"
    [ -f "$keys/keychain-password" ] || (umask 077 && openssl rand -hex 24 >"$keys/keychain-password")
    password="$(cat "$keys/keychain-password")"
    [ -f "$keychain" ] || security create-keychain -p "$password" "$keychain"
    security set-keychain-settings "$keychain"
    security unlock-keychain -p "$password" "$keychain"
    if ! security find-identity -p codesigning "$keychain" | grep -q "Isocast Test Signing"; then
        work="$(mktemp -d)"
        cat >"$work/cert.cfg" <<EOF
[req]
distinguished_name=dn
x509_extensions=ext
prompt=no
[dn]
CN=Isocast Test Signing
[ext]
basicConstraints=critical,CA:false
keyUsage=critical,digitalSignature
extendedKeyUsage=critical,codeSigning
EOF
        openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout "$work/key.pem" -out "$work/cert.pem" \
            -days 3650 -config "$work/cert.cfg" 2>/dev/null
        export_password="$(openssl rand -hex 12)"
        openssl pkcs12 -export -legacy -inkey "$work/key.pem" -in "$work/cert.pem" -out "$work/id.p12" \
            -passout "pass:$export_password" 2>/dev/null ||
            openssl pkcs12 -export -inkey "$work/key.pem" -in "$work/cert.pem" -out "$work/id.p12" \
                -passout "pass:$export_password"
        security import "$work/id.p12" -k "$keychain" -P "$export_password" -T /usr/bin/codesign >/dev/null
        security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$password" "$keychain" >/dev/null
        rm -rf "${work:?}"
    fi
    # codesign only finds identities in keychains on the search list.
    if ! security list-keychains -d user | grep -q "$keychain"; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC2046
        security list-keychains -d user -s $(security list-keychains -d user | tr -d '"') "$keychain"
    fi

    sh "$(dirname "$0")/testmac-bridge.sh" install >/dev/null
    echo "tools ready: $(rustc --version), $(ffmpeg -version | head -n 1 | cut -d' ' -f1-3)"
}

desktop() {
    user="$(id -un)"
    IFS= read -r password
    [ -n "$password" ] || { echo "desktop: pass the user's new password on stdin" >&2; exit 2; }

    # EC2: the APFS container may start at the AMI's size; grow it to the
    # volume (newer AMIs already have; diskutil then refuses, harmlessly).
    disk="$(diskutil list physical external | awk '/^\/dev\// { print $1; exit }')"
    container="$(diskutil list physical external | awk '/Apple_APFS/ { print $NF; exit }')"
    if [ -n "$disk" ] && [ -n "$container" ]; then
        yes | sudo diskutil repairDisk "$disk" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        sudo diskutil apfs resizeContainer "$container" 0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    fi

    # Set once: changing an existing password needs the old one.
    dscl . -authonly "$user" "$password" 2>/dev/null || sudo dscl . -passwd "/Users/$user" "$password"
    sudo launchctl enable system/com.apple.screensharing
    sudo launchctl load -w /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.screensharing.plist 2>/dev/null || true
    sudo sysadminctl -autologin set -userName "$user" -password "$password" 2>/dev/null || true
    # sysadminctl can leave out /etc/kcpassword (seen on EC2 macOS 26 and 27),
    # and loginwindow then stops at the login screen: write it ourselves (the
    # password XORed with loginwindow's fixed key, null-padded to 12 bytes).
    if ! sudo test -s /etc/kcpassword; then
        printf '%s' "$password" | /usr/bin/python3 -c '
import sys
key = [125, 137, 82, 35, 210, 188, 221, 234, 163, 185, 31]
data = list(sys.stdin.buffer.read())
data += [0] * (12 - len(data) % 12)
sys.stdout.buffer.write(bytes(b ^ key[i % len(key)] for i, b in enumerate(data)))
' | sudo tee /etc/kcpassword >/dev/null
        sudo chmod 600 /etc/kcpassword
        sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow autoLoginUser "$user"
    fi
    sudo pmset -a sleep 0 displaysleep 0 disksleep 0
    defaults -currentHost write com.apple.screensaver idleTime 0
    sysadminctl -screenLock off -password "$password" 2>/dev/null || true
    df -h / | awk 'NR == 2 { print "disk: " $2 " (" $4 " free)" }'
    echo "rebooting into the desktop session"
    sudo shutdown -r now
}

case "${1:-}" in
tools) tools ;;
desktop) desktop ;;
*)
    sed -n '2,18p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# Check an installed isocast .deb (CI, on a clean machine): the engine
# starts without OpenH264 and doctor says how to get it, the per-user
# command installs it, a 5 s recording of test sources completes through
# the CLI, and purging the package leaves the user's data alone.
#
#   packaging/deb/test-installed.sh SETUP_TOML DEB
#
# The Ubuntu 24.04 package has the browser helper: its AppArmor profile is
# a conffile, AppArmor (where it runs) has it loaded after install and
# after reinstalling the .deb over itself (the upgrade path of the
# maintainer scripts), and it is unloaded and gone after purge. The Debian
# 12 package has none (GTK 4.8; it needs 4.10), and doctor says so.
set -eu
setup=${1:?usage: packaging/deb/test-installed.sh SETUP_TOML DEB}
deb=${2:?usage: packaging/deb/test-installed.sh SETUP_TOML DEB}
sudo=$(command -v sudo || true)
step() { printf '\n== %s\n' "$*"; }
# AppArmor can load profiles here (not in a container without it).
apparmor() {
  [ "$(cat /sys/module/apparmor/parameters/enabled 2>/dev/null)" = Y ] &&
    command -v apparmor_parser >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
    $sudo test -r /sys/kernel/security/apparmor/profiles
}
loaded() { $sudo cat /sys/kernel/security/apparmor/profiles | grep -q '^isocast-browser '; }
helper=
[ -x /usr/bin/isocast-browser ] && helper=1
case $(dpkg-query -W -f='${Version}' isocast) in
*~ubuntu*) [ -n "$helper" ] || { echo "the Ubuntu package has no /usr/bin/isocast-browser" >&2; exit 1; } ;;
*~debian12) [ -z "$helper" ] || { echo "the Debian 12 package has isocast-browser (it needs GTK 4.10)" >&2; exit 1; } ;;
esac

step "installed files"
dpkg -L isocast | grep -E '^/usr/(bin|share/(applications|icons|doc))/' | grep -v '/$' | sort
for exe in isocast-media isocast isocastd isocast-ui isocast-openh264-install; do
  command -v "$exe" >/dev/null || { echo "missing $exe on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
done
# Only the per-user command's name may mention it (Cisco's licence is
# CISCO_H264_LICENSE.txt).
if dpkg -L isocast | grep -i openh264 | grep -v -x /usr/bin/isocast-openh264-install; then
  echo "the package contains OpenH264" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ -n "$helper" ]; then
  step "browser helper's AppArmor profile"
  test -f /etc/apparmor.d/isocast-browser
  dpkg-query -W -f='${Conffiles}' isocast | grep -q /etc/apparmor.d/isocast-browser ||
    { echo "the profile isn't a conffile" >&2; exit 1; }
  if apparmor; then
    loaded || { echo "AppArmor hasn't loaded isocast-browser" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "AppArmor: isocast-browser loaded"
  else
    echo "AppArmor isn't running here: the profile is installed, not loaded"
  fi
fi

step "upgrade path: the package installed over itself"
$sudo dpkg -i "$deb" >/dev/null
dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}\n' isocast
if [ -n "$helper" ] && apparmor; then
  loaded || { echo "AppArmor lost isocast-browser on reinstall" >&2; exit 1; }
  echo "AppArmor: isocast-browser still loaded"
fi

step "doctor without OpenH264"
rm -f "$HOME"/.local/lib/isocast/libopenh264-*.so
doctor=$(isocast doctor 2>&1 || true)
printf '%s\n' "$doctor"
printf '%s\n' "$doctor" | grep -q 'codec: OpenH264' || { echo "doctor didn't report the missing OpenH264" >&2; exit 1; }
printf '%s\n' "$doctor" | grep -q 'isocast-openh264-install' || { echo "doctor didn't name isocast-openh264-install" >&2; exit 1; }
if [ -z "$helper" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$doctor" | grep -q 'GTK 4.10' || { echo "doctor didn't say browser sources need GTK 4.10" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

step "isocast-openh264-install"
isocast-openh264-install
doctor=$(isocast doctor 2>&1 || true)
printf '%s\n' "$doctor" | grep -F "Cisco's OpenH264 2.6.0 (" || { echo "doctor didn't select the installed Cisco binary" >&2; exit 1; }

step "apply the test setup"
isocast apply --revision 0 "$setup"

step "app snapshot (offscreen, no display server)"
# The app's own runtime libraries (Vulkan, Skia, fonts) from the
# package's Depends alone.

# Install Isocast on macOS

Isocast requires an Apple-silicon Mac and macOS 14 or later.

1. Open the signed Isocast DMG and drag **Isocast** onto **Applications**.
2. Eject the DMG and open **Isocast** from Applications. macOS may ask you
   to confirm opening an app downloaded from the internet.
3. Follow the welcome screen to choose your sources. **Isocast Engine**
   requests camera, microphone and Screen & System Audio Recording access
   when you choose to grant it. Allow only the inputs you want to use.
   Screen-recording access may require restarting the engine (the app
   offers this; the CLI command is `isocast restart`).

The engine ships inside the app. No Rust, Homebrew, developer tools, or
separate daemon installation is needed. Permission status and next steps
are also available with `isocast permissions --json`. Synthetic sources
work without capture permissions.

## Command line

The command is `/Applications/Isocast.app/Contents/MacOS/isocast`. To put
it on your PATH without administrator access:

```sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
ln -s /Applications/Isocast.app/Contents/MacOS/isocast "$HOME/.local/bin/isocast"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
isocast --version
```

Add the `export PATH=…` line to `~/.zshrc` to keep it for new terminals.
The symlink command refuses to replace an existing command; inspect an
existing installation before changing it. Keep the app in Applications:
the symlink follows app updates and the CLI launches its bundled engine.

Run `isocast --help` for commands, `isocast mcp` for the MCP server. Normal
app, CLI and MCP sessions share the same engine and setup.

Isocast updates itself (from 0.0.2 on): it checks once a day and asks
before installing; **Isocast › Check for Updates…** checks now, and
Settings › General › Updates turns the daily check off. An update never
installs while isocastd records (or is paused), streams, exports or feeds
the virtual camera: it waits, then stops the engine and relaunches the
app on the new version. If you quit with **Keep Recording** while an update
is downloaded, it installs as the app closes and the engine finishes on
the old version; the next launch restarts it once it is idle.
`isocast status` shows which engine runs (`Engine: isocastd 0.0.3 (build …)`).

## Delete Isocast

Isocast Virtual Camera is a camera extension that stays in macOS when the
app goes to the Trash (macOS keeps listing it until it's removed). If you
started the virtual camera, remove it first:

1. In Isocast, open the gear beside **Virtual Camera** in the Controls dock
   and click **Remove Virtual Camera…** (or run `isocast vcam remove`).
2. Enter an administrator password when macOS asks.
3. Quit Isocast and move it to the Trash.

If macOS says a restart finishes the removal, keep Isocast until you have
restarted. Starting the virtual camera again installs it again. Your
recordings, setups and settings are not removed; they live in your
recordings folder and `~/Library/Application Support/Isocast`.

## Release maintainers

`scripts/release.sh --dry-run` prints the local build/sign/DMG workflow
(until the Sparkle public key is committed it says it skips that check;
real Developer ID builds stop on it, docs/releasing.md step 5).
Run without that flag to prepare a Developer ID-signed app and DMG. This
step requires the signing identity but no notarization credential or upload.
Gatekeeper should report **Unnotarized Developer ID** until finalization.
Use `--ad-hoc` for local packaging tests (not eligible for notarization/drafts).
Use a new `--output DIRECTORY` for each build; artifacts are never overwritten.
Version comes from `[workspace.package].version` in `Cargo.toml`.
Each build also stamps one numeric `CFBundleVersion` into the app, helper
and embedded daemon metadata (`ISOCAST_BUILD_VERSION`, else the current
Unix timestamp), independently of that product version.

Signing uses the login keychain's Developer ID Application identity and the
existing `isocast-notary` notarytool profile. First use of the signing key
may prompt its owner; approve it yourself, then retry if the 90-second
signing timeout was reached. Passwords are never read or written by the script.

Only the engine and CLI get hardened-runtime exceptions:

- `device.camera`: AVFoundation camera/capture-card recording.
- `device.audio-input`: microphone and audio-interface recording.
- `cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory`: Wasmtime 49's compiled plugin code
  uses `mmap` then `mprotect(RX)`. The narrower `cs.allow-jit` applies to
  `MAP_JIT`, which this Wasmtime version does not use. It is not sufficient
  here, so it is not added. There is no library-validation bypass, debugger
  entitlement, sandbox, or separate screen-capture entitlement.

The UI has hardened runtime without exceptions. Camera/microphone usage
strings and screen-capture guidance are included in both app plists. The
production UI has ID `dev.isocast.release`. The helper retains the engine's
canonical `dev.isocast.isocastd` ID so the virtual-camera extension recognizes
its signed producer. Engine privacy grants may carry over from a development
build signed by the same Apple team.

The engine helper carries the virtual camera's system extension; the first
**Start Virtual Camera** asks macOS to activate it, and **Remove Virtual
Camera…** deactivates it (see `docs/virtual-camera.md`).

The native Slint UI is the default, controlled by the one `app_target`
assignment in `scripts/release.sh`. `ISOCAST_APP_TARGET=isocast-app` opts
into the retired web UI explicitly, matching `scripts/app-dev.sh`.
The three executables retain distinct names even on case-insensitive disks.

Once per signing Mac, the owner restores the notarytool profile interactively
(notarytool prompts for Apple ID and an app-specific password; do not put
the password in a command or file):

```sh
xcrun notarytool store-credentials isocast-notary --team-id 9G68SMNHEU \
  --keychain "$HOME/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db"
```

After verifying the prepared app/DMG on a test Mac, finish those same binary
bytes and create the draft with one command:

```sh
scripts/release.sh --notarize --draft-release --output /path/to/verified/output
```

`--notarize` copies the prepared app into `OUTPUT/notarized/`, notarizes and
staples it, repacks the DMG containing that stapled app, and signs/notarizes/
staples the DMG. It never recompiles or re-signs the executables. The saved
product version, UI target and executable/plist hashes pin the build even
if the checkout changes. Strict signatures, both tickets, Gatekeeper and
the app mounted from the final DMG are rechecked. The final SHA-256 is
computed **after** stapling. Prepared originals remain in OUTPUT.

Submission ids and archive hashes are saved before waiting. Wait calls are
bounded to 60 seconds with progress every 20 seconds; a pending submission
resumes on the same command. If upload ended without an id, inspect the
notarytool history before removing the named `.submitting` marker and retrying;
the script refuses a blind duplicate upload. An interrupted signing step can
also resume. A stale `.release-lock` after a hard kill requires checking that
the previous process is gone before removing it.

`--draft-release` uploads only verified notarized output and its checksum
to a **draft** on `anomalyco/isocast`, with a short user-facing alpha summary
and that repo's main as its tag target. It reuses a matching draft and verifies both GitHub asset digests;
published releases or mismatched assets are refused. No git history is
pushed, release published, or repository setting changed. The draft URL is
saved in `OUTPUT/draft.json`. Use `--notarize` alone to stop before upload,
or `--draft-release` alone to resume after notarization. Both support
`--dry-run` against a prepared output directory.

Distribute `OUTPUT/notarized/Isocast-X.Y.Z-arm64.dmg` and its `.sha256` file.
Verify a download with `shasum -a 256 -c Isocast-X.Y.Z-arm64.dmg.sha256`
beside the DMG. App and DMG accepted receipts remain in `OUTPUT/notarized/`.

For GitHub Actions, API-key notarization, temporary signing keychains and
the protected release environment, see [Releasing Isocast](releasing.md).
The CI-specific runtime, generated-notes and draft-replacement options are
explicit; the local defaults above are unchanged.

# GPU path research (for tasks 3.1–3.6)

Research done 2026-10-11 from crate sources (wgpu 30.0.1, wgpu-hal 30.0.1,
objc2-core-video 0.3.2, objc2-metal 0.3.2, png 0.18.1). Nothing here was
built yet; verify as the tasks are done.

## Crates

- `wgpu = { version = "=30.0.1", default-features = false, features = ["std", "parking_lot", "metal", "wgsl"] }`.
  `wgpu::hal` is re-exported. wgpu-hal 29+ uses objc2-metal 0.3 / objc2 0.6,
  the same family as the rest of the repo (≤28 used `metal`-rs; most examples
  online are for that). Pin the version: hal APIs change between releases.
- objc2-core-video features `CVMetalTexture`, `CVMetalTextureCache`,
  `objc2-metal`; objc2-metal features `MTLDevice`, `MTLTexture`,
  `MTLPixelFormat`, `MTLResource`.
- `pollster` (or `Waker::noop()`) for the adapter/device futures; `png` for
  snapshots.

## Device and wrapping Metal textures

```rust
let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(wgpu::InstanceDescriptor {
    backends: wgpu::Backends::METAL, ..wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle() });
let adapter = pollster::block_on(instance.request_adapter(&Default::default()))?;
let (device, queue) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
    required_features: wgpu::Features::TEXTURE_FORMAT_16BIT_NORM, // for 'x420'
    ..Default::default() }))?;
let mtl = unsafe { device.as_hal::<wgpu::hal::api::Metal>() }.unwrap().raw_device().clone();
```

An existing MTLTexture becomes a wgpu texture in two steps:
`wgpu::hal::metal::Device::texture_from_raw(raw, format, MTLTextureType::Type2D, 1, 1, CopyExtent{..}, drop_callback)`
then `device.create_texture_from_hal::<hal::api::Metal>(hal_tex, &desc, initial_state)`
(`initial_state`: `TextureUses::RESOURCE` for inputs, `COLOR_TARGET` for
outputs). `Queue::as_hal` gives the MTLCommandQueue and shared-event waits.

## CVPixelBuffer → MTLTexture without copying

One `CVMetalTextureCache` per device; per plane
`CVMetalTextureCache::create_texture_from_image(None, &cache, pb, attrs, mtl_fmt, w, h, plane, out)`,
then `CVMetalTextureGetTexture`. Use the plane's own width/height (never w/2:
odd sizes). Keep the CVMetalTexture and the frame alive in the hal texture's
drop callback: wgpu-core frees hal textures only after the submissions using
them complete, so lifetimes are exact. Call `device.poll(PollType::Poll)` and
`cache.flush(0)` every frame, and don't keep textures across frames (that
starves capture pools; ScreenCaptureKit's queue depth is 8).

| CV format | plane 0 | plane 1 |
|---|---|---|
| `BGRA` | `Bgra8Unorm` | — |
| `420v` / `420f` | `R8Unorm` | `Rg8Unorm` |
| `x420` | `R16Unorm` | `Rg16Unorm` (10 bits in the top of 16) |

## YUV → RGB (one shader, matrix as a uniform)

```wgsl
let ycc = vec3(textureSample(y_tex, s, uv).r, textureSample(c_tex, s, uv).rg);
return vec4(clamp(csc.m * (ycc - csc.off), vec3(0.0), vec3(1.0)), 1.0);
```

BT.709 (rows R, G, B; columns Y, Cb, Cr; WGSL is column-major, so transpose):

| | offset Y / C | Y | R←Cr | G←Cb | G←Cr | B←Cb |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 420v | 0.062745 / 0.501961 | 1.164384 | 1.792741 | −0.213249 | −0.532909 | 2.112402 |
| x420 | 0.062501 / 0.500008 | 1.168932 | 1.799744 | −0.214082 | −0.534991 | 2.120653 |
| 420f | 0 / 0.501961 | 1 | 1.5748 | −0.187324 | −0.468124 | 1.8556 |

Pick the matrix from the buffer's `kCVImageBufferYCbCrMatrixKey` attachment
(default 709).

## Canvas output

Render into an IOSurface-backed BGRA CVPixelBuffer from a pool (add
`kCVPixelBufferMetalCompatibilityKey`), imported with
`kCVMetalTextureUsage = ShaderRead | RenderTarget`, wgpu usage
`RENDER_ATTACHMENT | TEXTURE_BINDING | COPY_SRC`; that buffer goes straight
to AVAssetWriter. Better for 3.3: a final pass into a `420v`/`x420` buffer (Y
into the R8 plane, CbCr at half size into RG8), the encoder's native input.

## Pitfalls

- Declared wgpu usage must match the MTLTexture's usage; check with
  `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1` and `InstanceFlags::VALIDATION`.
- Keep the view format equal to the texture format; use `Bgra8Unorm`, not
  `…Srgb` (stay in 709 gamma).
- No `clear_texture` on imported textures (use `LoadOp::Clear`).
- Don't hand the output buffer to the writer before the GPU finished:
  `device.poll(PollType::Wait { submission_index, .. })` or
  `on_submitted_work_done`; pipeline 2–3 frames.
- IOSurface textures are not flipped: origin top-left, as in wgpu.

## Snapshots

The canvas is a CVPixelBuffer in shared memory: once its submission is done,
lock it read-only, copy rows (BGRA → RGB) and write a PNG with
`png::Encoder` (`Rgb`, 8-bit, fast compression). General fallback:
`copy_texture_to_buffer` (256-byte row padding), `map_async`, poll. Expose it
as a daemon method so the CLI and MCP `preview_frame` share it.

# Scenes-as-code research (phase 4)

Research done 2026-10-11 by reading crate sources (nothing built). Pin
versions; these crates change APIs often. Verify as each task is done.

## Layout (4.2): `taffy = "0.14.0"` (MIT)

- No `parse` feature (it pulls MPL-2.0 `cssparser`); map props ourselves.
- `TaffyTree::new()`, `new_leaf(Style)`, `new_leaf_with_context(Style,
  ctx)`, `new_with_children(Style, &[NodeId])`, `set_style`,
  `compute_layout_with_measure(root, Size { width:
  AvailableSpace::Definite(w), .. }, |inputs, id, ctx, style|
  taffy::compute_leaf_layout(inputs, style, |_, _| 0.0, |known, avail|
  measure(ctx, known, avail)))`, `layout(id).location/size`.
- Prop mapping: `size: Size<Dimension>` (width/height), `inset:
  Rect<LengthPercentageAuto>`, `position: Position::{Relative, Absolute}`,
  `flex_direction`, `justify_content: Option<JustifyContent>` (consts like
  `JustifyContent::SPACE_BETWEEN`), `align_items`, `gap:
  Size<LengthPercentage>` (width = column gap), `padding`, `margin` (auto
  works), `aspect_ratio: Option<f32>` (width / height), grid via
  `display: Display::Grid`, `grid_template_columns: vec![fr(1.0), ..]`.
  `percent()` takes 0..1.
- Pitfalls: `location` is relative to the parent; absolute children are
  placed in their direct parent; default display is flex (decide whether
  scene children default to absolute); rounding is on by default
  (`disable_rounding()` for smooth morphs); flex items have automatic
  minimum sizes; lay out only on scene or data changes, never per frame.

## Text (4.3): `cosmic-text = "0.19.0"` (MIT OR Apache-2.0)

- glyphon 0.12 supports wgpu 30, but draws text in its own pipeline with no
  rotation, opacity, clipping or effects. Instead rasterise each text node
  once (cosmic-text `Buffer` + `SwashCache`) into its own RGBA texture,
  premultiplied, and draw it like an image; cache by (text, attrs, size,
  wrap width, raster scale).
- `FontSystem::new()` takes up to ~1 s (10× in debug): create one at
  daemon start, off the render thread. `Family::SansSerif` maps to "Open
  Sans", which macOS lacks: set `db_mut().set_sans_serif_family(..)`.
- Rasterise at the final pixel scale (the largest an animation reaches).

## Shapes (4.1)

- Rounded-box SDF (standard, as Inigo Quilez describes), per-corner radius
  by quadrant, antialiasing `clamp(0.5 - d / fwidth(d), 0, 1)`; border by
  `coverage(d + width)` (gives CSS's inner radius).
- Normalise radii on the CPU with CSS's overlap rule.
- Shadow: Gaussian with σ = blur / 2 via an erf approximation
  (Abramowitz & Stegun 7.1.27); not drawn under the box (CSS); quad margin
  ≥ 3σ + spread + |offset|.
- Premultiplied alpha throughout (`PREMULTIPLIED_ALPHA_BLENDING`).
- Keep `fwidth`/`textureSample` in uniform control flow (compute, then
  `select`). Pool uniform buffers (one dynamic-offset buffer per frame)
  once scenes have many nodes.

## TSX (4.8): `rquickjs = "0.14.0"` (features `loader`) + `oxc = "=0.153.0"` (features `transformer`, `semantic`, `codegen`)

- rquickjs: QuickJS-NG, 12 crates, pre-generated bindings for Apple
  targets (needs Xcode clang, not libclang). boa (145 crates) and
  deno_core (V8 download, 160 crates) are heavier.
- oxc: `Parser::new(&alloc, src, SourceType::tsx().with_module(true))`,
  `SemanticBuilder::new().build(&program).semantic.into_scoping()`,
  `TransformOptions` with `jsx.runtime = JsxRuntime::Classic`, `pragma =
  "h"`, `pragma_frag = "Fragment"` and the same pragmas under
  `typescript` (else the `h` import is elided), then
  `Transformer::new(..).build_with_scoping(..)` and `Codegen`.
- Evaluate in rquickjs with memory, stack and time limits
  (`set_interrupt_handler`); a prelude defines `h`, `Fragment` and the
  node components; local imports need a custom `Loader` that runs oxc;
  `Runtime` is `!Send` (dedicated thread). Return JSON via
  `ctx.json_stringify`.
- QuickJS has no fetch/WebSocket: expose Rust functions under the
  setup's permission list for 4.10.

## Images (4.4)

- `image = { version = "0.25.10", default-features = false, features =
  ["png", "jpeg"] }`: `ImageReader::open(p)?.with_guessed_format()?
  .into_decoder()?`, apply EXIF orientation, `into_rgba8()`, premultiply.
- SVG: `resvg = { version = "0.48.1", default-features = false, features
  = ["text", "system-fonts", "memmap-fonts"] }`; `usvg::Tree::from_data`,
  `resvg::render` into a `tiny_skia::Pixmap` (premultiplied) at the laid
  out size.
- usvg (fontdb 0.24) and cosmic-text (fontdb 0.23) can't share a font
  database.

## Licences

All permissive (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3 for tiny-skia, Unicode-3.0 for ICU
data). Avoid taffy's `parse` feature and deno_core (MPL-2.0 pieces).

## OBS effect filters (from obsproject.com/kb filter pages, 2026-10-11)

Public knowledge-base pages give setting names and defaults (rarely
ranges); the formulas are ours. Doc quirks noted where a default looks
wrong.

- Color Correction: Gamma −3..3 (0), Contrast −4..4 (0), Brightness −1..1

camera (it asks for your password, then an Approve click in System
Settings).

## 2. Before you record (5 minutes)

```sh
./target/release/isocast doctor   # permissions, encoders, devices, disk
./target/release/isocast tune     # does this Mac keep up with your setup?
```

Fix anything `doctor` flags. `tune` should say your setup fits.

## 3. The soak (2 hours)

Use your real setup: camera, microphone, display or window capture. Record
the program plus ISO files, and stream at the same time to a destination
you're happy to go live on.

While it runs, do what a normal session does, spread over the two hours:

- switch scenes, and take one live from Studio Mode;
- pause, then resume (Controls dock or your hotkey);
- add a marker; split once (`isocast split`);
- export a take to your editor (`isocast project export-nle`) and open it;
- leave it alone for a long stretch.

Watch the LCD's DROPPED counter and the status bar. Both should stay at 0.

## 4. After you stop

The REC details popover lists every file with frames, dropped and gaps.
To check the files themselves:

```sh
cd "<the take's folder>"
for f in *.mov *.mp4; do echo "$f"; ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_type,codec_name,width,height,r_frame_rate,duration -of compact "$f"; done
```

In every file the video and audio durations should match, and the
program's should match the time you recorded (minus pauses).

## 5. Crash recovery (10 minutes)

1. Start a recording, wait 30 s, then `pkill -9 isocastd`. Reopen the app:
   it says the take was interrupted, and the files play up to within about
   two seconds of the kill.
2. Same again, but pause first, then kill while paused. The note says the
   recoverable length is unknown; the files play up to about the last two
   seconds before the pause. Making this crash-proof is PLAN G.3b (after
   the alpha week).
3. Quit the app while recording: it asks before stopping.

## 6. When something's wrong

Help > Report a Bug… builds a report: a GitHub issue body and a zip of logs
and system details, with stream keys and tokens removed. Review the
preview, then press **Send Report**: it files the issue on GitHub for you
and uploads the zip privately (only maintainers can download it), then
offers Open Issue. Nothing is sent until you press Send Report. **Save Zip
Only** keeps the report on your Mac instead. If sending fails, the zip is
saved and Open GitHub Issue lets you file it by hand.

## What passes

- 0 dropped frames over two hours on your Mac, in every file and the
  stream;
- every file plays and its audio and video stay in sync;
- the crash tests recover what they say they do;
- the workflows above work without surprises (anything that surprised
  you is a bug report).

# Motion testing

How Isocast checks that what you drag follows the mouse, every frame,
without glitches, and without a person watching. It came from GitHub #24
(dragging dock splitters and resizing canvas items lags behind the mouse
and glitches, worse while recording).

```sh
scripts/motion.sh                         # the standard suite, headless, on this Mac
scripts/motion.sh --scenario canvas-corner --variant recording
scripts/motion.sh --clock lockstep --no-timing   # what CI runs
scripts/motion.sh --suite scripts/motion/controls.toml   # the harness's own controls
scripts/motion/compare.py OUT_A OUT_B            # two lockstep runs must be identical
ISOCAST_TESTMAC=isocast-m2-b scripts/testmac.sh gui 'scripts/motion.sh --window --bin target/release'
```

Results go to `target/scratch/motion/<time>/` (or `--out DIR`):
`summary.md` and `summary.json` for the suite, and per run
`<scenario>@<variant>/result.json`, `frames.jsonl` (one line per frame) and
`sheet.png` (the frames around the worst moment). `scripts/motion.sh` exits
0 when every run passed (a control: came out as its `expect` says), 3 when
one failed, 1 when one couldn't run. Only this invocation's runs count
(`runs.tsv`, and results stamped with its `MOTION_INVOCATION`): a result
left in the folder by an earlier run never stands in for one that failed
to run. One run at a time: the script holds an OS lock (flock) on
`$TMPDIR/isocast-motion.lock` for its whole life, so a crash frees it; the
next run first ends every process a crashed run left (its UIs, recorded
in the work folder's marker, then its engine and log relay), then empties
the folder. Outputs in `--out` (runs.tsv, each run's json and log, the
summaries) are written to a new temporary file and renamed into place;
a target that is a symlink or not a plain file is refused. Every engine the script starts is shut down (and TERM/KILLed if
it lingers) on normal exit, failure, Ctrl-C and SIGTERM; only SIGKILL of
the script itself can leave one.

## Three layers

| Layer | Where | What it drives | What it sees | Catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Headless, lockstep | CI, any Mac | the real Slint interface, offscreen, Slint pointer events, each at its own instant on a virtual clock the whole interface reads; after each input every call is answered and the picture shows the newest setup at the asked size before the frame is drawn (an engine infinitely fast in virtual time) | the interface's state, every frame's pixels (GPU readback), calls to the engine | anything structural: an edge that doesn't follow the pointer, frames of lag built into the design, jumps back, blank frames, flicker, too many engine calls. Deterministic (same pixels every run, checked), so it can gate a PR. A wait over 2 s makes the run invalid (it fails), never a drawn frame. |
| Headless, realtime | any Mac | the same, frames paced on the wall clock, the engine running as it does | the same, plus the engine's real round trips | lag and stalls from the engine (edits in flight, frames late), idle and while recording. Depends on the machine: a report, not a gate. |
| Real window | test Macs | `isocast-ui` in a window, real macOS mouse events | a second engine recording the window at 60 fps, cursor included | end to end: macOS events → winit → Slint → Core Animation layers → the screen. What a person sees. |

The headless layers run the real app code: `isocast-ui --motion` builds the
same `AppWindow` and `App` as the window does and talks to a real
`isocastd`. Only the platform is different: an offscreen window adapter
whose clock moves only when the runner says so (Slint's timers and
animations follow it, and so does everything the app times itself through
`src/clock.rs`: edit pacing, gesture tails, held frames, the LCD, meters), and the preview in its
portable mode (`--preview image`: the engine's frames as Slint images) since
there are no Core Animation layers offscreen. The real-window layer covers
the layers path.

## Scenarios

Suites are trusted developer input, but the harness still keeps them in
their box: scenario names are plain (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) because
they name the run's folder, which must be a plain child of `--out`; the
harness removes only the files it writes there (never recursively); `state`
steps come from an allowlist that only changes what the window shows or
the isolated engine's live setup (no file import/export, settings,
streaming or bug reports); and `isocast-ui --motion` refuses to run unless
`ISOCAST_SOCKET` and `ISOCAST_SETUP` point it at an isolated engine
(scripts/motion.sh sets them). The work folder is only emptied if its name
starts with `isocast-motion`, it isn't a symlink, and it carries the
marker the script writes.

A suite is TOML (`scripts/motion/suite.toml`, the standard one):

```toml
[defaults]
size = "1280x800"        # window points
scale = 1
fps = 60                 # the virtual display
picture = "engine"       # engine: the daemon's frames; test: a stand-in drawn from the box
clock = "realtime"       # or lockstep
variants = ["idle", "recording"]

[defaults.thresholds]
gap_pt_p95 = 2.0
lag_frames = 1
jump_back_frames = 0
stall_frames = 2
black_frames = 0
flicker_frames = 0
frame_ms_max = 16.7

[[scenario]]
name = "splitter-scenes"
target = "splitter:0"
before = []              # --state steps first, e.g. select-first-item, snap:off
steps = [
  { press = "target", ms = 50 },
  { move = [120, 0], ms = 600, easing = "ease-in-out" },
  { move = [-120, 0], ms = 600, easing = "ease-in-out" },
  { release = true, ms = 100 },
]
```

Steps: `press` (`"target"`: the target's grab point, or `[x, y]`), `move`
(by `[dx, dy]`) or `to` (`[x, y]`) over `ms` at `hz` events a second
(default 120, like a mouse) with `easing` (`linear`, `ease-in-out`,
`ease-out`), `release`, `wait`, `wheel` (`[dx, dy]` over `ms`), `key`, and
`state` (any `--state` the snapshot mode knows, for menus, dialogs,
toasts, Studio Mode's take…). Variants: `idle`, and `recording` (the
program and two ISO files of synthetic sources, started through the
Controls dock as a person would).

Targets, and how each is found in a frame:

- `splitter:N`: the Nth column splitter, left to right. State: the
  `ColumnSplitter` element's position (Slint's element search). Pixels: its
  1 px hairline (`Theme.line`), followed from frame to frame along a row
  through the docks.
- `row-splitter`: above the docks. State: the `RowSplitter` element. Pixels:
  the edge's profile down a column, taken at rest and matched each frame.
- `canvas-corner`, `canvas-move`: the selected item (the setup's magenta
  block, or the test picture's verdigris item with `picture = "test"`).
  State: the newest setup's box; the box drawn for the frame shown; the
  drag-test outline. Pixels: the item's right (or left) edge in the
  picture, along a row through the item where the frame shows it (found
  again each frame).
- `none`: no tracking, for scenarios that only check flicker and blank
  frames.

The standard suite: the Scenes|Sources splitter, the Mixer|Transitions
splitter (it resizes the dock after it), the splitter above the docks (it
resizes the preview, and with it the engine's frames), a canvas
bottom-right corner resize, and a canvas move (fixed in October, the
control). Each idle and while recording.

## What a run records and checks

Per frame (`frames.jsonl`): the pointer and whether it is pressed; the
edge in the interface's state, in the box drawn and in the pixels; the
interface's own time for the frame (inputs, timers, updates) and its
drawing time; how long it waited for the engine; redraws Slint asked for;
calls to the engine made in the frame and their size; engine frames
received and the setup revision they show; blank and black frames; tiles
(16 points) that went back to how they were two frames before.

Frame 0 is drawn before any input. Where the edge should be: at each
press, wherever it was in the frame before; from then to the frame with
the release (at the release's own position) moved as far as the pointer
has moved since the press; held after. Each gesture is measured from its
press to a third of a second after its release. Checks (`result.json`,
each against the suite's threshold):

- **coverage** (always, no threshold): a tracked target missing from any
  frame of a gesture, an unknown state, no gesture at all, or (lockstep)
  the engine not catching up fails the run. A measurement that couldn't
  be made is never a pass;
- **gap** (window points, `gap_pt_*`) between that and the edge on
  screen: median, p95, max;
- **gain** (`gain_off_by` against `gain_tolerance`): the edge's travel
  over the pointer's travel through the gesture, from the rest frame (1
  follows, late or not; 0.5 is the #24 splitter);
- **lag** (frames): the delay that best lines the edge up with the pointer,
  and the gap left after it (`residual_pt_p95`: wrong place, not late).
  Always reported and checked, whatever the gain;
- **jump-backs**: frames where the edge stepped back against the pointer
  by more than a device pixel;
- **stalls**: frames where the pointer (after the lag) has moved more than
  1.5 device pixels since the edge last moved and the edge didn't move. An
  edge drawn on the pixel grid moves in whole pixels, so a slow drag
  isn't a stall;
- **black/blank frames**: the picture black, or the window one colour;
- **flicker**: A-B-A tiles while the pointer goes one way (where it turns,
  positions repeat by design; within two frames of a press or release the
  interface changes state). Tiles that do it at rest (a blinking light) are
  found in 1.5 s of calibration first and left out, and so is the dragged
  object's own area (its texture moving can repeat a tile; whether it
  keeps up is the gap's business);
- **frame time** (`frame_ms_max`, `late_frames`): the frame finished: the
  interface's work, its drawing commands, the GPU's drawing and the read
  back (`cpu_ms` without the GPU is reported apart). Wall time, so only on
  local runs; CI passes `--no-timing`. Wall numbers live under
  `result.json`'s `wall`.

The same checks run on the interface's state (`in_state`) and the drawn box
(`drawn_box`), so a failure says where the lag comes from: the state
following the pointer but the pixels not (drawing, engine), or the state
itself wrong (the interface's logic). On failure, `sheet.png` shows twelve
frames around the worst one, cropped where the pointer went, with the
pointer (red cross), where the edge should be (cyan) and where it was
found (yellow). `--frames` writes every frame's crop (for a video), and
`--dump-frames 10,11` whole frames.

## Controls

`scripts/motion/controls.toml` checks the harness itself: runs whose
verdict is known. A good drag, a slow drag (under a pixel a frame), a
diagonal drag and a press with motion batched into its first instant, on
the offscreen test picture (drawn from the box, so they follow by
construction), must pass; the good drag with an injected fault must fail:
`inject = "lag:3"` (inputs reach the app three frames late), `"jump:20"`
(one frame's pointer 30 points off), `"blank:20"` (one frame not drawn),
`"freeze:15"` (ten frames of moves never reach the app). A control
expected to fail names the checks it must fail (`expect_failing`), so it
can't pass by failing for another reason. A release followed at once by
hovering far away must pass (the expectation holds at the release's own
position). The real-window analysis has its own controls on known rows:
`scripts/motion/window.py --selfcheck` (follows, 4-frame lag, frozen edge,
half speed, missing frames).
The splitter on main (#24) must fail too, until it's fixed. Run it after
any change to the harness.

## Determinism

Lockstep runs of the same build must draw the same pixels.
`scripts/motion/compare.py` compares two or more output folders frame by
frame (pixels hashed, positions, revisions, calls) and result by result,
leaving out only wall-clock numbers. What it took: the virtual clock
through the app (src/clock.rs), each input at its own instant, waiting for
every call and for the engine frame of the newest setup at the asked size,
replies applied before events of the same batch (two connections race),
the engine's live readouts (status, CPU) stilled, revisions counted from
the replay's start, and a fixed work folder (its path shows in the status
bar).

## Real window (test Macs)

`scripts/motion.sh --window` (scripts/motion/window.py), through
`scripts/testmac.sh gui`, holding the benchmark lock:

1. a test engine with `scripts/motion/setup.toml` and the app in a window
   (background mode, its own layout file);
2. the scenario run headless at the window's size, for the pointer's path
   and the grab point;
3. a second engine recording the window (window source, cursor shown,
   60 fps, ISO HEVC at high quality); with `recording`, the test engine
   records too;
4. the drag, as real macOS mouse events: `scripts/motion/pointer.swift`
   posts the whole path at 120 Hz with each event's host time when the
   process may post events (Accessibility); otherwise cua-driver (which has
   Accessibility on the test Macs) makes one straight drag of the
   scenario's first move;
5. the recording read frame by frame: the edge against the pointer (a
   frame of the drag where either isn't found makes the measurement
   invalid; frames keep their places, so lag is in capture frames). With
   cua-driver the pointer is the cursor in the same captured frame, so no
   clocks need lining up (end-to-end gap and **gain**: how far the edge
   moves per point the pointer moves); with pointer.swift, against the
   posted events through the host clock in the recording's manifest
   (`host_time_ns`), good to about a frame.

Measured so far: column splitters. Not yet: the row splitter (no tracker in
the window recording) and the canvas (the captured cursor sits on the
white corner handle, which the cursor finder would take for it; with
pointer.swift's event log it wouldn't need the cursor).

## CI

The `motion` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (macOS 15 arm64, GitHub-hosted,
read-only token) runs on pushes to main and on pull requests that touch
`crates/isocast-ui/`, `scripts/motion.sh`, `scripts/motion/` or ci.yml
(other pull requests skip its steps and pass, so it can be required). It
builds `isocast`, `isocastd` and `isocast-ui` (release), then

```sh
scripts/motion.sh --suite scripts/motion/controls.toml --no-timing   # the harness's own controls
scripts/motion.sh --clock lockstep --no-timing                       # the standard suite
```

and uploads the output folders as `motion-results`. It is a real gate:
lockstep draws the same frames on any machine (the virtual clock drives
the interface, the engine is waited for after each input, a 2 s wait makes
the run fail as invalid) and frame times aren't checked. The standard suite
has open issues, recorded in `scripts/motion/suite.toml` as `expect =
"fail"` with exactly the checks each fails; the job fails if any run's
failures differ from that (a regression, or a fix whose line wasn't
updated).

## Layout audit (#107)

`scripts/layout-audit.py` draws every screen offscreen (the main window,
Studio Mode, the vertical canvas, Multiview and projector windows, every
Settings page, the Properties and
other dialogs, menus, toasts, first launch, OBS import, Optimize, and
recording and streaming states; `list` shows them) at eight window sizes
from 900x600@2 to 3440x1440@1 plus a tall one, and a width sweep (900, the
window's minimum, to 2700 points) for the main screens, each against an engine of its own with
the synthetic setup. Then one Claude Haiku 5.5 checker per picture, 12 at
once, looks at it and answers through a validated `deliver_layout` tool:
"ok", or issues with a kind, a severity and a pixel box. Each checker's
OpenCode session is deleted after it answers (`--keep-sessions` keeps
them), so a run doesn't fill your session list. It runs in the
same isolation as the visual judge (a fresh copy of
`scripts/layout-audit/checker`, an empty global config, a read-only folder
with just that picture). The report (`report.html`, `report.md`,
`report.json`) groups pictures by screen, draws the boxes, and merges an
issue seen at several sizes ("at widths <= 1280"). It exits 1 on any
high-severity issue. Small models make mistakes, so a person (or a
coordinating agent) triages the flagged pictures before filing anything;
`calibrate` checks that deliberately broken pictures get flagged.

```sh
scripts/layout-audit.py run --bin target/release --out /tmp/layout   # ~500 pictures
scripts/layout-audit.py run --bin target/release --out /tmp/layout \
    --views 'settings-*' --sizes 900x600@2,1440x900@2 --sweep none
scripts/layout-audit.py check --out /tmp/layout --only 'settings-*' --recheck
scripts/layout-audit.py calibrate --bin target/release --out /tmp/layout-cal
```

## Prior art, and what was taken

- **Slint's testing backend** (`i-slint-backend-testing`): element search by
  type and accessible name, mocked time. Taken: the element search, to
  find splitters by type (debug info is already on for `--a11y`), and a
  platform whose clock only moves when told. Not its window adapter: it
  doesn't draw, and the pixels are half of what's checked.
- **Chromium's input latency and frame pacing** (event-to-frame latency
  traced per input, dropped/janky frames in frame sequences, smoothness
  metrics): the per-frame record of which input a frame shows, latency in
  frames rather than milliseconds, and checking dropped frames apart from
  latency.
- **Apple Instruments, Animation Hitches** (hitch time ratio; a commit
  hitch vs a render hitch): the split between the interface's own work per
  frame and its drawing, and the idea of naming where a late frame came
  from (state vs pixels vs engine).
- **Flutter `integration_test` and `FrameTiming`** (build and raster time
  per frame, `traceAction` around a scripted gesture, percentiles in a
  summary): scripted gestures over a real app with per-frame timings
  summarised as p50/p95/max, and timings as a report rather than a gate on
  shared runners.
- **Playwright tracing** (an action timeline with snapshots before and
  after each action): every run keeps its frames' facts and a picture of
  the moment it went wrong, so a failure can be understood from the
  artifact alone.

## Gotchas

- Slint's `TouchArea` reports `mouse-x` relative to where the area is
  *now*. A splitter that moves with the drag and computes its size from
  `mouse-x - pressed-x` feeds its own movement back: it settles at half
  the pointer's distance (#24, measured both headless and in a real window).
- 4:2:0 video can't be cropped to an odd height (`ffmpeg crop` fails
  quietly in a pipe); the window recording's levels differ from the
  theme's (`#242424` on `#121212` came out `#141414` on `#080808`), so lines
  are found by contrast.
- The test Macs' desktop bridge may not post events (no Accessibility):
  pointer.swift says so and window.py falls back to cua-driver.
- A relative recording folder resolves against the engine's working
  directory: motion.sh writes the work folder's absolute path into the
  setup.

name: Engine Bench

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'crates/isocast-engine/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-daemon/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-protocol/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-platform-*/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-client/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-cli/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-plugin/**'
      - 'Cargo.*'
      - 'scripts/bench.py'
      - 'scripts/e2e.py'
      - '.github/scripts/bench_report.py'
      - '.github/workflows/bench*.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: bench-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  compare:
    # Fork pull requests only. Lanes' pull requests (ci/<lane>, scripts/pr.sh)
    # are qualified on real hardware through hw-batch instead: a 90-minute
    # macOS job per lane PR would starve CI's runners.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0
      ISOCAST_SIGN_IDENTITY: '-'
      HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
      PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check architecture
        run: |
          test "$(uname -m)" = arm64
          echo "ISOCAST_SCRATCH=$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Merge base
        run: |
          base="$(git merge-base "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_SHA")"
          echo "BASE_SHA=$base" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          git worktree add --detach "$RUNNER_TEMP/base-src" "$base"
      - name: Rust toolchain
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal
          rustup default stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2
        with:
          save-if: false
      - uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4
        with:
          path: ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew
          key: ffmpeg-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('.github/workflows/e2e.yml') }}
          restore-keys: ffmpeg-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: FFmpeg
        run: brew list ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1 || brew install ffmpeg
      - name: Probe hardware
        run: python3 scripts/e2e.py --capabilities --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/capabilities.json"
      - name: Build base and head release binaries
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin/base" "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin/head"
          # Same target directory/toolchain/profile, with each binary frozen before the next build.
          export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target"
          cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path "$RUNNER_TEMP/base-src/Cargo.toml" -p isocast-daemon -p isocast-cli
          cp target/release/isocastd target/release/isocast "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin/base/"
          cargo build --locked --release -p isocast-daemon -p isocast-cli
          cp target/release/isocastd target/release/isocast "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin/head/"
      - name: Three interleaved base/head pairs per scenario
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/bench_report.py run --work "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench" \
            --head "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin/head/isocastd" --base "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin/base/isocastd" \
            --cli "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin/head/isocast" --pr "$PR" --head-sha "$HEAD_SHA" --base-sha "$BASE_SHA" \
            --capabilities "$RUNNER_TEMP/capabilities.json" --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench-report.json"
      - name: Comparison table
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench-report.json" ]; then
            python3 .github/scripts/bench_report.py render "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench-report.json" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo '## Engine benchmark failed before measurements; see job logs.' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
      - name: Numeric report for trusted publisher
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: engine-bench-report
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/bench-report.json
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14
      - name: Raw measurements and logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: engine-bench-evidence
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/capabilities.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/bench/**/results.jsonl
            ${{ runner.temp }}/bench/**/bench.log
            ${{ runner.temp }}/bench/**/*.session.json
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

name: Refresh appcast notes

# Replace a PUBLISHED release's appcast.xml with one that embeds
# docs/releases/X.Y.Z.md from main (#106). The DMG is downloaded and checked
# (GitHub digest, .sha256, its EdDSA signature in the published appcast),
# never rebuilt or re-signed; only appcast.xml is uploaded. See
# docs/releasing.md, "Fix a published release's update notes".
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Published version (X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z) whose appcast notes to refresh'
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

# The Release workflow's group: never refresh while a release is drafting.
concurrency:
  group: isocast-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Without secrets or approval: the version, its notes file on main, and a
  # published (not draft) release with exactly the DMG, checksum and appcast.
  preflight:
    if: github.repository == 'anomalyco/isocast' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check the version, its notes and the published release
        id: version
        env:
          INPUT_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          version="${INPUT_VERSION#v}"
          [[ "$version" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo 'version must be X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z' >&2; exit 1; }
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          python3 scripts/release-finalize.py --refresh-appcast "$version" --dry-run \
            --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/refresh-appcast"

  refresh:
    needs: preflight
    runs-on: macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Ryan approves; the Sparkle key exists only here.
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ needs.preflight.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Sparkle tools (pinned, hash-verified)
        run: scripts/sparkle/sparkle.sh path
      - name: Check the Sparkle update signing key
        env:
          SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY }}
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import base64, binascii, os, sys
          try:
              key = base64.b64decode(os.environ.get('SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY', '').strip(), validate=True)
          except (binascii.Error, ValueError):
              key = b''
          if len(key) not in (32, 96):
              sys.exit('SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY is missing or not a Sparkle EdDSA private key (generate_keys -x); its value is not logged')
          print('Sparkle signing key present')
          PY
      - name: Verify the published DMG and appcast, regenerate with the notes, replace appcast.xml
        env:
          SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SPARKLE_ED_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: python3 scripts/release-finalize.py --refresh-appcast "$VERSION" --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/refresh-appcast"
      - name: Summary (both feeds)
        if: always()
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import os
          from pathlib import Path
          root = Path(os.environ['RUNNER_TEMP']) / 'refresh-appcast'
          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY'], 'a') as out:
              out.write(f"## v{os.environ['VERSION']} appcast.xml\n\n")
              for label, path in [('Published before (the rollback)', root / 'original' / 'appcast.xml'), ('Regenerated (uploaded only if the step above passed)', root / 'appcast.xml')]:
                  if path.exists():
                      out.write(f'### {label}\n\n```xml\n{path.read_text()}\n```\n\n')
          PY

name: Engine E2E

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'crates/isocast-engine/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-daemon/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-protocol/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-platform-*/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-client/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-cli/**'
      - 'crates/isocast-plugin/**'
      - 'examples/plugins/**'
      - 'Cargo.*'
      - 'scripts/e2e.py'
      - 'scripts/pacing.py'
      - 'scripts/pacing-probe.m'
      - '.github/workflows/e2e.yml'
  push:
    # The train tests the merged tree; a lane can opt in early with ci.sh --full.
    branches: [main, 'ci/batch-*', 'ci/full/*']
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: e2e-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  # Per branch, so lanes never cancel each other; a lane's newer candidate
  # (or a pull request's newer push) cancels its older run, main's never.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/ci/') }}

jobs:
  # Decides whether this change needs the engine run end to end
  # (.github/scripts/ci_gate.py); its summary says why.
  gate:
    name: what to run
    # Same-repo snapshots are tested by the train. Keep fork PR checks.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      e2e: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.e2e }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 0 || 2 }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: python3 .github/scripts/ci_gate.py e2e

  e2e:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.e2e != 'skip'
    # GitHub-hosted arm64 only. Untrusted PR code never reaches test Macs.
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0
      # full, or warm (main: restore the cache; build only if it missed).
      MODE: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.e2e }}
    steps:
      - name: Gate mode
        # Fail closed: a job that runs without a mode from the gate would
        # skip every step and pass without checking anything.
        run: |
          case "$MODE" in
            full|warm) ;;
            *) echo "::error::the gate gave this job no valid mode ('$MODE'); not passing without running"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check architecture
        run: |
          test "$(uname -m)" = arm64
          echo "ISOCAST_SCRATCH=$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Rust toolchain
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install stable --profile minimal
          rustup default stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2
        id: cache
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      - if: env.MODE == 'full'
        uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4
        with:
          path: ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew
          key: ffmpeg-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('.github/workflows/e2e.yml') }}
          restore-keys: ffmpeg-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: FFmpeg
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        run: brew list ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1 || brew install ffmpeg
      - name: Frame oracle selftest (fixture, decoder and the oracle's own rules)
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        # The hosted loss rules pass VM losses but still fail a broken frame,
        # a frozen source, a 2-frame A/V offset and a missing ISO.
        run: python3 scripts/e2e.py --selftest --work "$RUNNER_TEMP/selftest"
      - name: Build release engine
        if: env.MODE == 'full' || steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        # The CLI too: the frame oracle reads a scene feed with it (masks B5).
        run: cargo build --locked --release -p isocast-daemon -p isocast-cli --bins --examples
      - name: Diagnose timers, process policy, Metal and compositor pacing
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        timeout-minutes: 11
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          python3 scripts/pacing.py --work "$RUNNER_TEMP/pacing" \
            --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/pacing.json"
      - name: Measure VM hardware and qualify 720p30 (program, two ISOs and RTMP)
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        run: |
          python3 scripts/e2e.py --hosted --capabilities --keep-failures \
            --work "$RUNNER_TEMP/e2e" --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/capabilities.json"
      - name: End-to-end scenarios
        if: env.MODE == 'full'
        run: |
          python3 scripts/e2e.py --hosted --capabilities-from "$RUNNER_TEMP/capabilities.json" \
            --keep-failures --work "$RUNNER_TEMP/e2e" \
            --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/e2e-report.json"
      - name: Job summary
        if: always() && env.MODE == 'full'
        run: |
          if [ -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/e2e-report.json" ]; then
            python3 scripts/e2e.py --summary "$RUNNER_TEMP/e2e-report.json" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          elif [ -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/capabilities.json" ]; then
            python3 scripts/e2e.py --summary "$RUNNER_TEMP/capabilities.json" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo '## Engine E2E: build/startup failed before hardware qualification; see logs.' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
      - name: Report and failing files
        if: always() && env.MODE == 'full'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: engine-e2e
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/e2e-report.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/capabilities.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/pacing.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/pacing
            !${{ runner.temp }}/pacing/**/Dev.app/**
            !${{ runner.temp }}/pacing/**/probe
            ${{ runner.temp }}/e2e
            !${{ runner.temp }}/e2e/**/Dev.app/**
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

name: Nightly soak

# Hours of recording on synthetic sources, looking for slow failures that
# the short E2E scenarios can't see: crashes, hangs, leaks, stalled writes,
# broken takes and stream disconnects. See "Nightly soak" in docs/archive/2026-10-22/delegator-handbook.md (section 6).
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '23 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      hours:
        description: 'Hours to record (at most 5.25; the job limit is 6 h including the build)'
        required: false
        default: '5'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: nightly-soak
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  soak:
    # GitHub-hosted arm64 only: free for public repos, never our own Macs.
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 350
    env:
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0
      HOURS: ${{ inputs.hours || '5' }}
    steps:
      - name: Job start and architecture
        run: |
          test "$(uname -m)" = arm64
          echo "SOAK_JOB_START=$(date +%s)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "ISOCAST_SCRATCH=$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          if ! printf '%s' "$HOURS" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$' ||
             ! awk -v h="$HOURS" 'BEGIN { exit !(h > 0 && h <= 5.25) }'; then
            echo "::error::hours must be a number above 0 and at most 5.25"
